goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:24 interpolates raw site-setting host value into INSERT SQL; a host with a quote breaks the migration and is an injection vector; should use quote/parameterization

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration reads the existing site setting value (embeddable_hosts[0]['value']), splits it into records, and then builds SQL via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. Since `h` is inserted inside single quotes without escaping/quoting, any host value containing a `'` will break the SQL, and a crafted value could inject additional SQL at migration time. This is a concrete, verifiable issue in the diff; it should use connection.quote / parameterization / insert helpers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 validation regex requires a TLD of 2-5 letters, rejecting valid hosts like localhost, IP addresses, and longer TLDs (.museum, .technology)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In app/models/embeddable_host.rb the validation `\.[a-z]{2,5}` restricts the top-level domain to 2–5 letters. This will reject real, common domains with longer modern TLDs (e.g. `.museum`, `.technology`). It also rejects non-TLD hosts like `localhost` and raw IPs because the regex requires a dot + alpha TLD. This is a concrete behavior directly implied by the regex in the diff.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:197 for *_ids arrays, _lookupSubType may return undefined for missing ids, leaving undefined entries in the hydrated array; the hydrated || [] fallback never triggers since map always returns an array

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` the new plural branch (`/(.+)_id(s?)$/` with `m[2]`) does `const hydrated = obj[k].map(id => self._lookupSubType(...))` and then assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []`. Since `Array#map` always returns an array (truthy), the `|| []` fallback will never be used. If `_lookupSubType` returns `undefined`/`null` for an id that can’t be hydrated (which the prior singular-path guarded against via `if (hydrated) { ... }`), the resulting hydrated array will contain `undefined` entries rather than omitting them or producing an empty array. That’s a concrete behavioral regression introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:197 hydration fires on any key ending in _ids even when the value is not an array, so .map throws

adjudication.rationale: The change in store.js adds handling for keys ending in `_ids` and assumes `obj[k]` is an array by calling `obj[k].map(...)` without a type/null guard. However, the diff does not show any payload/schema where a `_ids` field would be non-array; the newly introduced usage (`has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids`) would normally serialize to an array (possibly empty) of ids. So while the code would throw if some `_ids` value were null/non-array, that scenario is not demonstrated or implied by the diff, making the finding speculative rather than a verifiable defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6:22 type.replace('_', '-') only replaces the first underscore, so multi-underscore type names would not match the admin list

adjudication.rationale: It’s true that `String.prototype.replace('_','-')` only replaces the first underscore, but in this diff the only admin model types being matched are `plugin`, `site-customization` (would come from `site_customization`, only one underscore), and `embeddable-host` (from `embeddable_host`, only one underscore). There’s no multi-underscore admin model shown here that would fail to match, so the finding is hypothetical rather than a verifiable defect introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:10 update action (PUT /admin/customize/embedding) is a no-op that returns current state, so the client's saveChanges silently does nothing

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` action that simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and does not read params or persist anything. On the client side, `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defines `saveChanges()` which calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, which would hit the PUT `/admin/customize/embedding` route. Given the server-side `update` is a no-op, that client “save” operation would succeed but not change state, matching the finding. (Even if the current template doesn’t wire up `saveChanges`, the endpoint/action pair is still verifiably non-functional.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:3 and embedding_controller.rb:3 have redundant before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff on an Admin::AdminController subclass that already enforces admin; ensure_staff is looser than the parent's admin check and misleading

adjudication.rationale: Both controllers do explicitly add `before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff`, but the diff does not show what `Admin::AdminController` enforces. The claim that the parent "already enforces admin" and that `ensure_staff` is "looser" (and therefore misleading) depends on code outside the diff and is not verifiable from the changes shown. Even if redundant, this is at most a minor clarity/style concern rather than a clear defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:38 sets category from Discourse.Category.findById(categoryId) after save, but when categoryId is null the server substituted uncategorized_category_id, so the UI shows no category until reload

adjudication.rationale: In `embeddable-host`’s `save()` action, the client sends `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')`. For a new host `categoryId` starts as `null` (it is only set in `edit()` from `host.category.id`, and new records have no category). On the server, `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` explicitly substitutes `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` when `category_id` is blank. However, after a successful save the UI sets `host.category = Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))`; if `categoryId` was `null`, this assigns `undefined` even though the server just saved/returned a non-null `category_id`. Because the serializer only returns `category_id` (not an embedded category object), `host.category` won’t be auto-hydrated, so the category badge can be empty until reload.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/*_controller_spec.rb for new controllers only assert inheritance; no coverage of create/update/destroy, invalid host handling, nil id, or the category fallback

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds two new controller specs: `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb`. Both contain only a single example asserting the controller is a subclass of `Admin::AdminController`, and they do not exercise any of the controllers’ actions (`create/update/destroy` in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, `show/update` in `Admin::EmbeddingController`) or edge cases (e.g., missing/invalid `id` in update/destroy, validation failures, or the category fallback to `uncategorized_category_id` implemented in `save_host`). This is directly verifiable in the added spec files and represents a real gap in test coverage introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/locales/server.en.yml removed embeddable_hosts and embed_category setting descriptions but remaining 'EMBEDDING ONLY' descriptions still imply configuration via site settings with no pointer to the new admin UI

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` site settings (and their server locale descriptions) because configuration is moved to the new `EmbeddableHost` model/admin UI. The remaining settings in `config/site_settings.yml` under `embedding:` (e.g., `feed_polling_enabled`, `embed_truncate`, etc.) are still real site settings, so keeping their `EMBEDDING ONLY` descriptions in `config/locales/server.en.yml` is accurate and does not create a correctness/bug issue. The proposed finding is essentially a documentation/UX suggestion (add a pointer to the new UI), not a verifiable defect introduced by this diff.
